basic_details.major_restrictions: Peace and Conflict Resolution, International Development, Human Rights, Public Policy, Global Public Health, Environmental Peacebuilding, International Relations.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~130 fellowships awarded globally per year (50 Master's degrees, 80 Professional Development Certificates)
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open global merit pool; Pakistan has a strong history of fellows endorsed by local Rotary districts (typically 2 to 5 awardees/yr)
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: 15 to 24 months for Master's degree; 1 year (including online modules and on-site intensive) for Professional Certificate

nationality_requirements: Open to citizens of all countries (except active Rotary club members or direct descendants of Rotarians)
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: Bachelor's degree (16 years education) with strong academic standing.
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Minimum 3.00 / 4.00 CGPA; practical field experience and leadership impact are weighted heavily alongside academic grades.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Background in social sciences, public policy, international relations, law, journalism, or related fields.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduated and currently working in peacebuilding, development, or public service.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Minimum 3 years of full-time professional experience in peace, development, or conflict prevention for Master's; minimum 5 years for Professional Certificate.

english_proficiency.notes: Proficiency in English required (IELTS 7.0+ or TOEFL 90+); second language proficiency evaluated favorably.

eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: Fluency in English; proficiency in a second international language is advantageous.
eligibility_requirements.gender_specific_requirements: Equal opportunity; diversity and female community leadership strongly encouraged.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Proven leadership and dedicated commitment to peacebuilding and community transformation.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Active Rotary members, honorary Rotarians, and their spouses or lineal descendants are ineligible.

tuition_fee.details: 100% full tuition and mandatory academic fees paid directly to host university.

admission_application_fee.details: Application and university administrative costs reimbursed or waived under Rotary partnership.

accommodation.details: Room and board covered comprehensively via living stipend or direct university housing.

monthly_stipend.details: Monthly stipend to cover rent, utilities, food, and personal living expenses (~USD $1,800 to $2,400/month depending on host city / ~PKR 500,000 to 670,000/month).

airfare.details: Round-trip economy international airfare between home country and host university.

visa_fee.details: Visa application processing fees reimbursed upon presentation of receipts.

health_insurance.details: Comprehensive student medical and emergency repatriation insurance provided.

food_allowance.details: Included within monthly room and board stipend.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Course books and study materials allowance provided.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Fully funded Applied Field Experience (AFE) of 2-3 months during summer break (travel, housing, and living stipend fully covered).
research_funding_conference_grant.amount: Full funding for summer field practicum

travel_transit_allowance.details: Travel transit allowance provided for relocation.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: Rotary Peace Fellowship Online Application Portal
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Create an account on the Rotary International Peace Fellowship application platform during the open window.
step_by_step_workflow: 1. Review eligibility criteria and ensure 3+ years full-time peace/development work experience (January).
2. Connect with a local Rotary Club or District in Pakistan for initial consultation and endorsement inquiry.
3. Complete the online Rotary Peace Fellowship application.
4. Upload transcripts, essays, CV, and two professional/academic recommendation letters.
5. Submit application to local Rotary District by May 15.
6. Attend district interview (virtual or in-person) by July 1.
7. Rotary District submits endorsement to The Rotary Foundation.
8. Central Rotary Peace Center committee announces fellowship winners in November.
9. Selected fellows apply to host university for academic admission (November-January).
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Scholarship awarded first by Rotary International; fellow then applies to assigned host Rotary Peace Center university.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by 2 referees (1 professional supervisor, 1 academic or civic leader).
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Essays detailing peacebuilding vision, professional leadership experiences, and how the fellowship will advance peace initiatives in your community.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Essays explaining specific issues in peace and development you plan to address during your studies and summer field experience.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Professional CV highlighting peace, NGO, human rights, public sector, and community leadership roles.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Rotary District endorsement interview conducted in June; central finalist video interview in September.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: GRE not required by Rotary; university may require language test.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Authenticated copies of university transcripts and degree certificates.

1 professional reference validating peace/development work + 1 academic/leadership reference
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: From NGO directors, UN supervisors, or professors

important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Very structured annual timeline; applications submitted 15 months prior to academic commencement.

selection_process_and_weights.work_experience_weight: 30% (Proven record in peacebuilding, development, and community impact)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 10% (Clarity of vision and commitment to Rotary ideals)
selection_process_and_weights.interview_weight: Crucial stage during district and global panels
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: District Rotary Committee, International Rotary Foundation Trustees, and Faculty Selection Board of host Peace Centers.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: District endorsement interview -> Global screening by Rotary Trustees -> Finalist placement at host Rotary Peace Center.

competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~50 Master's fellowships and ~80 certificate fellowships annually
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Mid-career leaders with 4-8 years of on-the-ground experience in disaster relief, refugee rehabilitation, human rights advocacy, mediation, or public sector governance.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Pakistani fellows include NGO founders, UN field officers, civil servants, and investigative journalists.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: United States, Pakistan, Colombia, Kenya, Nigeria, India, Afghanistan, Myanmar, Uganda.

fake_websites_and_scams: Scam portals soliciting endorsement fees: rotary-peace-fellowship-portal.org, peace-scholars-fund.com.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Applying for Rotary Peace Fellowship is 100% free of charge. Never pay any Rotary club or district for an endorsement.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Endorsements must be obtained directly through legitimate Rotary clubs; third-party agents have no standing.
itemized_hidden_out_of_pocket_costs: HEC and MOFA attestation of Pakistani degree documents (~PKR 15,000 to 25,000)
English language test fees (IELTS/TOEFL) if required by host university (~PKR 55,000 to 65,000)
Initial domestic travel expenses within Pakistan to attend Rotary District interviews
debunked_myths_and_misconceptions: MYTH: You must be a Rotarian to apply. (Truth: Rotarians and their immediate relatives are legally disqualified from applying; it is strictly intended for non-Rotarians).
MYTH: You need a degree in peace studies. (Truth: Candidates from law, engineering, computer science, journalism, medicine, and business with peacebuilding applications are welcome).
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Commercial sites suggest direct university application; Rotary requires fellowship selection first, followed by university placement.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Maintain good academic standing per host university graduate regulations.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time physical attendance; participation in annual Rotary Peace Conference.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Semi-annual progress reports submitted to The Rotary Foundation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Fellows are expected to dedicate full time to their academic studies and applied field experience; outside employment is discouraged.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: No binding service bond, but fellows commit to advancing peace and international cooperation throughout their careers.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.service_obligations_or_bonds: Commitment to lifelong membership in Rotary Peace Fellowship Alumni Association.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Funding terminated if fellow drops out, engages in academic misconduct, or fails to complete summer field experience.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_university: Strictly prohibited; fellows are assigned to a specific Rotary Peace Center.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Not permitted outside approved degree course.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: No extensions beyond the standard degree curriculum.
